response.sql: WITH manager_counts AS (SELECT p.throws, COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id) as manager_count FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON ma.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), shares AS (SELECT throws, manager_count, CAST(manager_count AS NUMERIC) / SUM(manager_count) OVER () as share FROM manager_counts), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM shares), filtered AS (SELECT s.throws, s.manager_count, s.share, oa.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE s.share > oa.avg_share) SELECT SUM(manager_count) as total_count, AVG(share) as average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) as average_excess FROM filtered

assumptions.assumption: If no hands have share exceeding the overall average share, the result is a single row with NULL values for all three columns. The request does not specify expected behavior for this edge case.

"the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share" refers to the overall average share computed before filtering (across all hands), not the average share within the filtered subset.
